pages.title: Patrols from large bases
pages.text: Larger surface and floating bases regularly launch a Flux Ship with a soldier at the controls. These scouts travel to another base or make a broad survey loop home.$(br2)This is separate from ordinary monster spawning. Lighting the ground does not prevent launches. Scouts start at least 128 horizontal blocks from players, and defeated base AIs stop sending them.$(br2)Only two scouts may stay near you. Further ships break off and take another route.$(br2)Scouts cruise about fourteen blocks above terrain, climbing over obstacles and banking through turns.

pages.title: Take cover
pages.text: A scout that spots you abandons its patrol to attack. It climbs and takes distance, turns the entire ship to aim its front cannon, then dives through a firing pass and pulls away for another run.$(br2)Scouts can also engage flying players and lead moving targets. The hull is indestructible, but half of a laser hit reaches the pilot. Defeat the pilot and the ship gently descends, ready to recover.$(br2)Solid roofs and walls break its sight and stop its shots. It searches near your last sighting rather than following hidden movement. Stay unseen for a full minute to make it resume its route.

pages.title: Passing traffic
pages.text: A ship reaching its destination leaves when players are far away. If you are nearby, it starts another flight instead.$(br2)First launch opportunities begin within a second. Bases up to 896 blocks away are considered, prioritizing those ahead of your flight path, with a default repeat delay of 10 to 20 seconds. Clear space and the two-scout limit still apply.

pages.title: Patrol frequency
pages.text: Scouts do not launch in Peaceful mode. Server owners can disable them with ai.scoutPatrols or adjust repeat delays with ai.scoutLaunchIntervalSeconds in the world's arienteworld-server.toml.$(br2)Existing worlds adopt the faster default and clear old launch waits automatically. Nondefault repeat intervals are preserved.
